title: Installation hook downloads and executes a remote script
risk: Installing the package runs a hook that downloads a script over plain HTTP and executes it with the installer's privileges, with no signature, digest, or source pinning.

evidence.description: postinstall runs node scripts/bootstrap.js during dependency installation.
The hook builds a shell command that curls a runtime-configurable HTTP URL and pipes it to bash.
No signature, checksum, or pinned version check appears on the download path.

trigger: Installation of the package, including as a transitive dependency, with no user interaction beyond the install command.
preconditions: The package manager runs install lifecycle scripts for this dependency.
The CDN host, DNS, or network path can be influenced by an attacker.
reachability: Reachable through the documented install path; no application-level input is required.
privilege: The installing user's identity, elevated when a global or system-wide install is run with administrator rights.

impact.summary: Arbitrary code executes on every machine that installs the package and can read local files and environment credentials and modify user state.
impact.blast_radius: Every install host, plus downstream consumers of artifacts produced on those hosts.

attack_chain: dependency resolution → postinstall → remote download over HTTP → shell execution → host and credential access
maliciousness_basis: The execution path is proven from repository evidence; no intent is inferred. Dynamic confirmation would require an isolated environment and was not performed.
remediation: Remove the install-time download and execution path, vendor the content, or verify a pinned digest or signature before execution and fail closed when verification fails.
validation: In a disposable sandbox with synthetic credentials and blocked egress, install the package and confirm the hook no longer downloads or executes remote content.
